requirements.discrimination: Returning before the dependency readiness barrier or swallowing startup failure fails the public construction assertions.
A dependency initialization failure must raise engine_unavailable at construction with a lifecycle error and remedy.
Removing each required public contract version must reject construction and close the incompatible runtime before caller work.
Caller, built-in, MCP, delegated and skill effects must obey explicit authority, and absence of authority must never infer allow.
An approval handler returning allow after cancellation cannot authorize the pending tool or change the authoritative cancelled terminal.
Denial and approval cancellation must produce rejected/cancelled; timeout, unavailable and malformed replies must produce their named failures without effects.
Closed and injected owned errors must match every shared code, category, message, remedy, retryability, correlation, details and extension field at method and terminal phases.
The same literal provider script must deliver the exact shared order of all eleven registered event types and an owned extension without merge, filtering or reordering.
Exact integers, native decimals, ids, nested strict JSON, ordered empty/text parts and owned additions must cross event and callback boundaries unchanged.
Shared literal turn/session corpora and full exact records reject differing run, resumed or forked results, missing/reordered events, altered failure codes, or fork history.
Removing each required public contract version must reject construction and close the incompatible runtime before caller work.
Repeated accepted cancellation must drain pending callbacks and provider work, start no new request or effect, and retain turn_cancelled.
False string spellings must reach the wire as false; JSON booleans preserve their value and ambiguous scalars/containers are refused.

Unknown accepted Responses fields must reach wire verbatim for the selected provider only; semantic overrides and unhonored settings must fail at construction, and retention opt-in cannot alter local resume.
Reversing any option, environment, file, or default precedence for provider/model/storage/workspace changes observed selections or session ownership.
Caller edits to instructions, tools, schema, model, approval policy, environment, or storage must not change later execution or transcript ownership.
A misspelled host key must identify itself and its nearest valid key, while seam variables must not become host-key errors.
Silently accepting unknown, excluded, or settings-only programmatic fields fails construction refusal before provider work.
Invalid input must raise at the method before a stream exists; post-start provider failures must be terminal AgentError records.
Both native method errors and terminal errors must preserve the complete shared record including optional correlation, exact nested details and owned additions.

Actual pre-turn, tool-resolution and terminal failures must use registered or owned codes, registered categories and valid error records; the same validator rejects corrupted unqualified codes and malformed owned names.
Repeated unchanged invalid option/input requests remain nonretryable and name the needed correction; full shared closed and retryable provider error remedies must remain actionable and unchanged.
Corrupted sequence, turn identity, event type, timestamp, or terminal brackets must fail the same validator used on public success, failure, rejection and cancellation streams.
Corrupted sequence, turn identity, event type, timestamp, or terminal brackets must fail the same validator used on public success, failure, rejection and cancellation streams.
Recoverable tool failures must remain truthful correlated results while execution continues; fatal provider failures must reach terminal rather than escape iteration.
Owned event names cannot act as registered terminal states; all unknown envelope/payload fields, including additive optional fields, must survive exact public delivery.
An orphan or duplicate tool result, missing resolution, or miscorrelated approval decision fails exact pair assertions, including during cancellation.
Strict JSON progress rejects nonfinite numbers, cumulative usage replaces prior snapshots, and the final payload remains the full result.
Flattened or reordered output parts and altered reasoning finals fail reconstruction from incremental events.

All eleven actual registered events and owned extensions must validate; corrupted unqualified or malformed owned names fail the validator, and progress or an owned terminal-like event cannot signal success.
Corrupted sequence, turn identity, event type, timestamp, or terminal brackets must fail the same validator used on public success, failure, rejection and cancellation streams.
Fresh versus resumed turns, including reopened durable sessions, must identify the actual configured provider/model selection.
All four terminal states must be reachable; success has no error, and accepted cancellation must retain turn_cancelled instead of approval_cancelled.
Unsupported roles, media, function-call structures, and empty combined input must fail at both methods before provider work, preserving first-turn eligibility.
Historical system/developer messages must neither replace configured instructions/tools nor grant authority denied by the host.
Dropping seed context on subsequent turns or duplicating it in a fork changes independently captured provider messages.
Durable, already-used, and inherited conversations must refuse replacement seeds; an empty ephemeral fork remains eligible.
Unsupported roles, media, function-call structures, and empty combined input must fail at both methods before provider work, preserving first-turn eligibility.
Unsupported roles, media, function-call structures, and empty combined input must fail at both methods before provider work, preserving first-turn eligibility.
Supplied history must not bypass busy or closed failures.
Seed roles and text parts must precede exactly one appended user message when content is present and no invented message when it is empty.
Imported messages must not create historical turns or usage; recorded input retains the seed and each real turn accounts only its scripted model work.
Mutating supplied history after acceptance must not change recorded roles, order, text, or content-part boundaries.
Imported messages must not create historical turns or usage; recorded input retains the seed and each real turn accounts only its scripted model work.
Independent agents constructed with distinct workspace/storage snapshots must not share session listings or conversation messages.
An active blocked session must not prevent another session progressing, and fork children must not mutate parent history.
Close must cancel active work, wait through cancelled caller waits and effect cleanup, and return only after paired resolutions and terminal.
Closing a session or its agent must reject every subsequent operation and readable session property with closed; repeated close remains harmless.
An explicit retention opt-in must still resume from complete local history through a newly constructed agent without provider conversation identifiers.

Native reasoning survives durable agent restart, bounds optional completed-turn age/size, and retains complete required active tool-round envelopes and function signatures. A strict native fixture rejects missing or truncated required reasoning before accepting tool results; all visible inputs and tool history remain intact.
Responses and subscription requests must explicitly disable retention and omit previous-response state unless store is deliberately enabled in host settings.
All provider families must replay prior input and tool results in new requests without relying on a previous response id or retained SDK session.
Session/turn refinements may only lower verified prices; above-ceiling delegated work and incompatible saved ceilings must fail before new work.
Provider lists, including one containing the aggregator, must fail before work; provider failures must not cause another selection or retry.
Independently recorded requests must use the selected primary model; Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini returning a substituted actual model must yield selector_rejected after one request.
Deleted durable state must disappear from listing and remain not_found on resume; deletion of a live handle must fail session_in_use.
A killed caller process must release ownership while completed input and reply survive entirely in local durable state; durable remains the default.
Resuming a closed ephemeral child must fail not_found even when it previously completed turns.
Fork must copy the parent snapshot once into a distinct UUIDv4 with inherited persistence and reject active parents without blocking other sessions.
Duplicate creation, unknown resume, and competing durable handles must produce already_exists, not_found, and session_in_use respectively.
Generated ids must be UUIDv4 and distinct while invalid uppercase, short, overlength and malformed caller ids are refused.
A busy session must reject rather than queue a second turn, and subsequent accepted turns must carry earlier context exactly once.
Storage overrides must determine durable session ownership after directory/environment changes, across create, checkpoint, fork, resume, and delete.
Traversal, uppercase, overlength and malformed slugs must fail; distinct valid workspaces must own independent session sets.
Buffering all events until the provider completes deadlocks the independent first-delta barrier and fails before the fixture releases completion.
Provider failure or premature provider EOF must yield a typed failure terminal preserving already observed output, with no retries.
Allowing a second consumer instead of stream_already_consumed fails the public iterator reuse case.
Built-in, caller, MCP, delegated and skill effects must remain visible and obey refusal; non-allow outcomes must not start effects and resolutions stay source-correlated.
Caller executors must receive decoded strict JSON with exact integers, the event call id, and its exact UTC deadline; nonfinite arguments must never execute.
Each actual caller, file and MCP effect must remain absent when its public tool_call is observed and wait for the subsequently released approval gate.

Python callback strings are the supported result channel: structured, wrong-id or duplicate-shaped return values are invalid, while immutable copied callback context cannot alter engine-assigned identity. Actual dead callbacks, invalid returns, reported failures and uncertain outcomes retain their distinct registered errors; duplicate/orphan observations fail the same pair validator.
Default tool errors terminate as failure, protocol failures remain fatal under continue, and accepted cancellation cannot become a recovery success.
The caller callback must execute in the host process exactly once, MCP in a distinct process exactly once, and the built-in effect must use its own executor.
One recorded model tool list must contain caller, built-in and MCP names; each source-named call must correlate to its one resolution.
Duplicate names, missing handlers, and invalid declarations must fail at construction without invoking an executor.
After uncertainty, new shell/write/caller/MCP/delegate/skill effects and pending approvals must be blocked; approved local inspection and already-running effects retain their rules.

A result past the ceiling must reach the model shortened, with one kept-of-total marker, truncated, and original_bytes; the 262144 default must bound an unconfigured result, None must carry the whole result unmarked, a result within the ceiling must stay unmarked, and zero, negative, boolean, string, and fractional ceilings must fail before provider work.

An absent tools list must offer all nine built-ins and an empty list none; a list must offer exactly its entries; a caller bash in a set without the built-in must execute with source caller; an unknown name must fail before provider work; skill commands must refuse to run without the built-in bash; BUILTIN_TOOLS must equal the nine names.
An unregistered recovery policy must fail before work and the default stop behavior must terminate reported failed/unknown effects.
Recoverable failed/unknown results must return to the same model turn without rewriting their outcome or dropping partial output/history.
Continue must not recover invalid callbacks/results, approval refusals, skill guard failures, or accepted cancellation.
Each call must have exactly one later correlated completed/failed/cancelled/unknown result, including callback cancellation and execution errors.
Missing or invalid schema dialects must fail; descriptive safety metadata must never act as an approval grant.

An external effect completing after its one Python callback reported uncertainty must never be retried or rewrite its unknown result/history. Public callbacks cannot submit result IDs or a second resolution; engine-assigned identity, single settlement, rejected duplicate/orphan observations, and continue restrictions are verified through the available callback channel.
Mutable turn identity or reused turn ids fails the immutable-record and distinct-turn assertions.
A separate run path that bypasses approvals or changes errors, content, or usage differs from the streamed terminal for the same scripted outcome.
Known cost must preserve exact native Decimal precision and USD identity; absent provider cost must remain unknown rather than zero.
Counters above 2^53, cache zero versus unknown, cumulative increments, and multiple actual selections must retain exact independent measurements.
The last replacement snapshot must follow output/model work, equal terminal usage, accumulate all requests and include delegated selections without fabricating unknown values.
Actual child model selections must be separately accounted for in final usage while above-ceiling delegated work is rejected before execution.

The capture must hold the session lifecycle and prompt events with fixture secrets redacted in replies and tool results while the model and transcript keep the actual tool output, append across resume, cover ephemeral and delegated work outside the session list, and its removal must leave history and the next turn unchanged.

A configured loopback destination must receive authenticated POST /events records for the session while a refused destination, an excluded destination, a foreign settings.yaml, and foreign AMPLIFIER_CONTEXT_INTELLIGENCE_* variables neither fail the turn nor receive anything; the environment form and malformed settings must be refused by field.

transcript.jsonl and metadata.json must appear only at workspaces/<workspace>/sessions/<id>/, messages past the last committed turn must stay invisible after resume, and a directory holding only a capture must never list or resume as a session.
